learning_outcomes.text: Knows the general principles of engineering design applied to machine elements.
Knows static and variable stresses and the safety criteria associated with these stresses.
Knows the constructive, functional, and dimensional typologies of threaded joints, belt drives, chain drives, and gear reducers.
Knows the function, behavior, and efficiency of mechanical transmissions in complex assemblies.
Has notions about technical execution and assembly documentation, according to engineering standards.
Applies engineering methods of design, dimensioning, and verification for various machine elements.
Performs functional and strength calculations and analyses for mechanical transmissions.
Uses experimental apparatus and stands for verifying theoretical hypotheses.
Develops engineering assembly projects, including constructive solutions, technical-economic comparisons, and functional justifications.
Drafts and supports coherent technical documentation, using symbols and specific norms for machine elements.
Assumes responsibility for the correctness of the design and calculation of machine elements.
Demonstrates autonomy in choosing and justifying constructive technological solutions.
Respects occupational safety norms, technical standards, and engineering requirements for precision and functionality.
Collaborates efficiently in laboratory and project work, assuming active engineering roles.
Demonstrates a critical and responsible attitude towards proposed engineering decisions.

syllabus_topics: Constructions. Forces and moments in threaded joints. Efficiency
Screws subjected to bending and transverse loads.
Planetary transmissions. Efficiency and specific problems of geometry and strength
Threaded joints. Constructive forms. Technical solutions (Laboratory)
Threaded joints. Initial tightening of screws (Laboratory).
Threaded joints. Screws subjected to transverse loads (Laboratory)
Ball screws. Analysis of specific parameters (Laboratory).
Project theme: screw lifting mechanism (car jack) (Project)
Choosing the constructive variant and comparisons (Project)
Design of the nut and support parts (Project)
Comparative technical and technical-economic analysis of possible variants (Project)
Preparation of execution and assembly documentation (Project)
teaching_methods: Visual materials (sketches, constructive models, technical images)
Direct and indirect exploration of technical reality
Presentation of real parts and analysis of their functioning in mechanical assemblies
Specialized laboratory with computing techniques, infography and videoprojector
Experimental stands and specific installations for the study of stresses, mechanical transmissions and various types of joints
assessment_rules: The final grade is composed of 60% for the final exam (oral and summative test), 15% for laboratory activities, and 25% for the project. A minimum score of 5 (likely out of 10) is required for each of these components. Conditions for passing include knowing the general principles of engineering design applied to machine elements and being able to draft and support coherent technical documentation using specific symbols and norms for machine elements. No explicit resit arrangements are mentioned.
